text:
maria-sales: Quick presales question — ACME Health wants a 6-week POC and is asking for recommended reserved GPU sizing + autoscale policy. Workload: chat completions + embedding lookups. Expected steady 180 rps, burst up to 1.1k rps for ~10min, avg request ~120 tokens. They’ll need VPC and SOC2 notes. Any blockers before I put this in the quote?

amina-solutions: Congrats on the lead! For planning: do we know concurrency per user and typical context length? those influence KV-warmup and batch sizing.

maria-sales: Concurrency roughly 2k concurrent users during peak, most chat sessions ~300 tokens context. They want 99.9% availability during business hours.

alex-eng-runtime: For 180 steady / 1.1k burst with ~120 tokens req, rule-of-thumb: target_rps_per_gpu 350 for natively quantized models. That suggests reserved pool ~4 GPUs to cover steady + safety, with autoscale up to 12 GPUs for burst headroom (use burst credits). Important: preheat window and KV warmup for chat context to avoid cold tail latency.

devon-sre: +1. Also recommend AZ spread (min_replicas per-AZ) and circuit-breaker to avoid a noisy-neighbor cascade. We use this minimal autoscale template in presales smoke tests: 

```yaml
autoscale_policy: 
  min_replicas: "2"
  reserved_replicas: "4"   # commit pool
  max_replicas: "12"
  target_rps_per_gpu: "350"
  scale_window: "60s"
  preheat_window: "5m"   # pre-warm KV cache
  cooldown: "90s"
  circuit_breaker_threshold: "95p_latency_ms:1200"
```

amina-solutions: For the POC we usually propose: 4 reserved GPUs + 8 burstable GPUs, 48hr monthly steady-run smoke with synthetic load to validate tail latency and billing. We’ll provide an infra runbook and the load script.

liam-pricing: Pricing note — 4 reserved GPUs (monthly) + burst usage billed at on-demand rate with a capped burst credit pool for the POC. I can bake that into the quote: estimated committed fee + $X/hr burst burn. Need expected burst minutes per month to firm numbers.

maria-sales: ACME expects ~6 hours/day of burst over 3 weeks in ramp. Is that feasible?

alex-eng-runtime: That’s fine if we include burst credits and preheat plan. Important to pin model quantization level for perf predictability (e.g., 4-bit int8-style quant). We should lock the model+quant profile in the offer.

sarah-security: On the SOC2/VPC/KMS front: they requested sub-processors list, encryption in transit+at rest, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for model access. For Private customers we can offer a sub-set in a VPC with HSM-backed KMS — but that’s an enterprise add-on. For the POC we can provide SOC2 docs, share a sanitized access log sample, and enable KMS with customer key in Dedicated.

maria-sales: Any technical blockers that would stop us from offering the 4 reserved + 8 burst config for the POC?

devon-sre: Operational checklist: 
- confirm AZ parity for reserved pool
- smoke test load generator + KV warmup script (we can reuse /tools/presales/poctest.sh)
- add alerting for queue-depth and GPU saturation to the runbook
- prepare rollback to smaller model variant if latency/regression observed

alex-eng-runtime: One more: tail-latency regression tests against a golden prompt set. If regression > 10% we fallback to smaller context model or increase GPUs. Also include explicit model-rollout pin in the config so POC uses same binary.

redwood-bot: Deploy job queued: presales-smoke-2026-06-14, ETA 20m.

amina-solutions: Proposed next steps: 
1) I’ll schedule a joint runbook + smoke test with ACME for next Tue (we need their IP ranges for VPC allowlist).
2) Devon will provision reserved pool + burst credits in sandbox and handover to SRE for monitoring config.
3) Liam will draft pricing line items (reserved + burst credits + private KMS add-on).
4) Sarah will attach SOC2 + dataflow doc and list of controls we can provide in POC.

maria-sales: Great — I’ll finalize questionnaire answers and confirm the runbook participants. One ask from legal: they want an explicit SLA for <10ms 50p gen latency during steady-state — is that realistic?

alex-eng-runtime: <10ms 50p is unrealistic for current gen chat models at that token size. We should re-scope SLA to 50p <250ms for steady or propose a distilled smaller model variant for strict latency. Recommend push-back: offer 100ms 50p for embeddings and 250ms 50p for chat in SLA.

liam-pricing: Counterpart for legal: if they want tighter SLA we need higher reserved commit (more GPUs + priority routing) and a premium SLA fee. I’ll model both standard and premium SLA pricing.

maria-sales: Perfect. I’ll update ACME and loop in legal. Thanks all — tagging next actions: @amina-solutions @devon-sre @liam-pricing @sarah-security

devon-sre: I’ll spin the sandbox pool and post the smoke test command and load profile to the runbook channel when ready.

sarah-security: I’ll prepare a short checklist they can attach to their questionnaire; will ping if they ask for on-prem option.

amina-solutions: I’ll schedule the test and share the load generator repo.

maria-sales: Closing loop here — will post customer confirmation and target dates once legal OK’s. :thumbsup:
